expectations: Be clear about how the work of your department improves the experience of scholars, families, and schools. Use their experience to help us understand what is working and what needs to change.
Know your work. Know your data.
Know the priorities, progress, and challenges in your department. Come ready to explain what the data tells us, whose experience may be different, and what we need to pay attention to next.
When you raise an issue, share what you know, what you have tried, and where you need help. We can work through the next step together. Raise concerns early enough for us to respond.
Understand how your decisions affect other teams. Involve the right people early, work through concerns directly, and take responsibility for the connections your work depends on.

Do what you say you will do. Make sure people know who is responsible and when to expect the next step. If something changes, communicate it. Return to the work and check whether it made a difference.
Build the capacity of your team
Make expectations clear, provide useful feedback, and create opportunities for people to learn and lead. Document the work so your team can carry it forward with confidence.

highlights.label: State & Federal Programs · Attendance
highlights.title: Attendance moving in the right direction
highlights.finding: 436 fewer scholars were chronically absent than in 2024–25. Attendance improved at 30 schools—eight more schools than the previous year.
highlights.meaning: Progress across schools gives us something to build on as we continue the Strive for Less Than 5 work.
highlights.context: The report still identifies 5,247 chronically absent scholars and a district rate of 40.0%. These figures do not establish the effect of any one intervention.
highlights.source: Chronic Absenteeism: End of Year Report · 2025–26 · page 1

highlights.label: Health Services
highlights.title: Helping scholars stay in school
highlights.finding: 47,859 of 53,010 recorded dispositions were returns to class.
highlights.meaning: School health care supports scholars in returning to learning.
highlights.context: Recorded dispositions, not unique scholars. Uses the district disposition table on printed page 5 (PDF page 8). The summary narrative cites a different denominator.
highlights.source: GRPS 2025–26 School Health Advocacy Report · printed page 5

highlights.label: Summer School
highlights.title: Two routes toward graduation
highlights.finding: High school scholars earned 83 credits in person and 64.5 credits through E2020.
highlights.meaning: Summer learning helped scholars make progress toward graduation.
highlights.context: Credit totals, not a count of unique scholars.

highlights.label: Counseling · Assessment & Evaluation
highlights.title: More scholars graduating on time
highlights.finding: The district graduation rate increased from 82.53% in 2024 to 83.22% in 2025: a gain of 0.69 percentage points.
highlights.meaning: A shared district result to build on through scholar planning, support, and review of school and scholar-group patterns.
highlights.context: Shared district outcome; not attributed to one department.

highlights.label: Social Emotional Learning · PBIS+
highlights.title: Building stronger Tier 1 practices
highlights.finding: Eight schools reached at least 70% on the Tier 1 Tiered Fidelity Inventory. The report records 27 completed inventories and a 60% average implementation score.
highlights.meaning: Use the TFI to identify the practices working in schools and the support each PBIS+ team needs next.
highlights.context: The school table supports eight scores at or above 70%; five are strictly above 70%. This measures implementation fidelity, not scholar outcomes. The report describes associations with attendance, behavior, and climate without establishing causation.
highlights.source: PBIS+ Installation Update · Tiered Fidelity Inventory Impact Report · pages 1–2
